The wind of the snow has left its storerooms because of its strength. There is a special wind in it, and what rises from it is like smoke; its name is hoarfrost.
The wind of the mist does not share their storerooms; it has a storeroom of its own, for its course is glorious in light and in darkness, in winter and in summer, and an angel is in its storeroom.

The wind of the dew lives at the ends of heaven and is joined to the storerooms of the rain. Its course is in winter and in summer, and its clouds and the clouds of the mist are joined; one gives to the other.

When the wind of the rain goes out of its storeroom, the angels come, open the storeroom, and lead it out. When it spreads over the whole dry ground, it unites with the water on the earth; and whenever it unites with the water on the earth . . .{f}
For the waters are for those who live on the dry ground; they are nourishment for the earth from the Most High in heaven. So there is a fixed measure for the rain, and the angels are in charge of it.
All this I saw near the Garden of the Righteous.
The angel of peace who was with me said to me, “These two monsters, prepared in keeping with the greatness of the Lord, will feed . . .{g}

so that the punishment of the Lord of Spirits may not come upon them for nothing. Children will be killed with their mothers, and children with their fathers. When the punishment of the Lord of Spirits rests on them, it will stay on them, so that the punishment of the Lord of Spirits may not be in vain. After that the judgment will take place in keeping with his mercy and his patience.”{h}

notes.text: In the life of Enoch: the date originally belonged to Noah (compare Gen 7:6, 11, where Noah is 600 at the flood); the editor who placed this Noah fragment here changed the name, but verse 8 still has Noah speaking of “my grandfather.” *The seventh month*: in the Jewish calendar Tishri, roughly September–October, the month of the Day of Atonement and Tabernacles; on the 364-day calendar of 1 Enoch and Jubilees, see the notes at chapter 72.
*Leviathan*: Hebrew *liwyatan*, perhaps “coiled one,” the sea monster of Job 41; Ps 74:14; 104:26; Isa 27:1. *Behemoth*: Hebrew plural of *behemah*, “beast,” meaning “the great beast” (Job 40:15–24).
*Dendayin*: the manuscripts vary (*Dendāin*, *Dâidâin*, *Dûidâin*). Perhaps a form of the desert “Dudael” (10:4), or of Nod “east of Eden” (Gen 4:16).
My grandfather: Enoch, grandfather of Noah's father Lamech; so the speaker here is Noah (see the note at verse 1). Enoch was “the seventh from Adam” (Gen 5:3–24; Jude 14).
Son of man: here simply “human being, mortal,” as in Ezekiel (Ezek 2:1).
The text is broken off here in all manuscripts.
Will feed: the text is broken. Later Jewish tradition held that Leviathan and Behemoth would be food for the righteous at the end (4 Ezra 6:49–52; 2 Bar 29:4).
The order and wording of verses 24–25 are confused in the manuscripts; this rendering follows the reconstruction generally adopted.

verses.text: In those days I saw long cords handed to those angels. They took wings for themselves and flew off northward.
I asked the angel, “Why have they taken those cords and gone?” He answered, “They have gone off to measure.”

The angel who went with me said,
“These will bring the measurements of the righteous
and the measuring lines of the righteous to the righteous,
so that they may lean on the Lord of Spirits’ name forever and ever.{a}

These measurements will bring to light every secret of the depths of the earth,
those swallowed up by the desert,
those eaten by wild animals,
and those eaten by the fish of the sea,
so that they may come back and find support
on the day of the Chosen One;
for no one will be lost before the Lord of Spirits,
and no one can be lost.”
All who are in the heights of heaven received a command, a power, one voice, and one light like fire.

With their first words they blessed that one,
and they praised and exalted him with wisdom,
showing wisdom in speech and in the spirit of life.

When he raises his face
to judge their hidden ways by the word of the Lord of Spirits’ name,
and their paths by the way of the just judgment of the Lord of Spirits,
then with one voice they will all speak and bless,
glorify, exalt, and hallow the Lord of Spirits’ name.

He will call the whole host of heaven, all the holy ones above, the host of the Lord—the cherubim, the seraphim, and the ophanim,{c} all the angels of power and all the angels of dominion—and the Chosen One, and the other powers that are on the dry ground and over the water.

On that day they will lift a single voice. They will bless, glorify, and exalt in a spirit of faith, of wisdom, of patience, of mercy, of justice and peace, and of goodness, and all will say together, “Blessed is he, and blessed be the Lord of Spirits’ name forever and ever!”

For the Lord of Spirits abounds in mercy and is patient;
all his works and all that he has made
he has revealed to the righteous and the chosen
in the Lord of Spirits’ name.

notes.text: Measurements... measuring lines: images of resurrection and restoration; compare Zech 2:1–5; Ezek 40:3; Rev 11:1.
Placed... on the throne: so some manuscripts; others read “The Lord of Spirits sat on the throne of his glory.”

Cherubim, seraphim, ophanim: classes of heavenly beings. *Cherubim* (Hebrew *keruvim*, meaning uncertain) guard Eden and the ark (Gen 3:24; Exod 25:18–22); *seraphim*, “burning ones” (Isa 6:2); *ophanim*, “wheels” (Ezek 1:15–21; 10:9–13). Compare 71:7.

verses.text: This is what the Lord commanded the kings, the powerful, the exalted, and those who inhabit the dry ground: “Open your eyes and raise your horns,{a} if you can recognize the Chosen One.”

The Lord of Spirits seated him{b} on his glorious throne,
and the spirit of righteousness was poured out on him.
The word of his mouth kills every sinner,
and all the lawless are wiped out before him.{c}

On that day all the kings and the powerful,
the exalted and those who hold the dry ground,
will rise up and see and know
that he sits on his glorious throne;
righteousness is judged in his presence,
and no false word is spoken before him.

Then pain will come over them
like that of a woman in labor
who struggles to give birth
when her child comes to the mouth of the womb.
The kings, the powerful, and all who possess the dry ground will bless, glorify, and exalt the one who rules over everything, who had been hidden.

The community of the chosen and holy will be sown,{e}
and all the chosen will stand before him on that day.

All the kings, the powerful, the exalted, and those who rule the dry ground
will fall face down before him,
worship him, set their hope on that Son of Man,
and beg him and plead for mercy from him.

But the Lord of Spirits will press them so hard
that they will rush from his presence;
their faces will be full of shame,
and darkness will pile up on their faces.

He will hand them over to the angels of punishment
to take vengeance on them,
because they oppressed his children and his chosen ones.

They will be a spectacle for the righteous and for his chosen ones.
They will rejoice over them,
because the anger of the Lord of Spirits rests on them
and his sword is drunk with their blood.{f}

The righteous and chosen will be saved on that day,
and from then on they will never again see the faces of the sinners and the lawless.

The righteous and chosen will have risen from the earth
and will no longer go about with downcast faces.

They will be dressed in garments of glory,
garments of life from the Lord of Spirits.
Your garments will not wear out,
and your glory will not fade before the Lord of Spirits.{g}

notes.text: Raise your horns: an idiom for showing strength or pride (Ps 75:4–5).
Seated him: so with a slight change; the manuscripts read “sat on.”
Compare Isa 11:2, 4; Ps Sol 17:24; Rev 19:15.

Son of a Woman: Ge'ez *walda be'si*, “son of a man” in most manuscripts; some read *walda 'eguāla 'emma-ḥeyāw*, “son of the offspring of the mother of the living,” that is, of Eve. See the note at 46:2.
Will be sown: that is, will be planted and grow; compare 10:16; 93:2, 5, 10.
Compare Isa 34:5–6; Deut 32:42.
Compare 2 Cor 5:2–4; Rev 3:4–5; 6:11.

verses.text: In those days the powerful and the kings who possess the dry ground will beg his angels of punishment, to whom they have been handed over, to give them a short break, so that they may bow in worship to the Lord of Spirits and acknowledge their sins to him.

They will bless and glorify the Lord of Spirits, saying:
“Blessed is the Lord of Spirits, the Lord of kings,
Lord of the powerful and Lord of the rich,
Lord of glory and Lord of wisdom.

Every hidden thing shines with your power from generation to generation,
and your glory endures forever and ever.
Your secrets are deep and past counting,
and your righteousness is beyond reckoning.

Now we have learned that we ought to glorify
and bless the Lord of kings, the one who is King over all kings.”

They will say, “If only we had a pause to glorify, give thanks,
and confess our faith before his glory!

Now we long for a little rest but do not find it;
we chase it but cannot catch it.
Light has gone from before us,
and darkness is our home forever and ever.

For we did not believe in him
or glorify the Lord of Spirits’ name;
our hope was in the scepter of our kingdom
and in our own splendor.

On the day of our suffering and distress he does not save us,
and we find no break in which to confess
that our Lord is faithful in all his deeds, his judgments, and his justice,
and that his judgments show no partiality.

We vanish from his presence because of our deeds,
and every one of our sins has been counted out exactly.”
Then they will say to themselves, “Our souls are stuffed with ill-gotten wealth, but it does not stop us from going down out of it into the flames of the torment of Sheol.”{a}

After that their faces will be filled with darkness
and shame before that Son of Man;
they will be driven from his presence,
and the sword will stay before him among them.
So says the Lord of Spirits: “This is the decree and the judgment against the powerful, the kings, the exalted, and those who possess the dry ground, in the presence of the Lord of Spirits.”

notes.text: The flames of the torment of Sheol: so some manuscripts; others read “the weight” or “the burden of Sheol.” Compare Luke 16:23–24.

verses.text: I saw other figures hidden in that place.
I heard the angel’s voice say, “These are the angels who came down to the earth, disclosed hidden things to humankind, and led human beings into sin.”
In those days Noah{a} saw that the earth had tilted and that its ruin was near.
He got up from there and went to the ends of the earth and cried out to his great-grandfather Enoch.{b} In an anguished voice Noah said three times, “Hear me, hear me, hear me!”
I said to him, “Tell me what is happening on the earth, that the earth is so battered and shaken, or I may perish with it.”
Just then there was a great upheaval on the earth; a voice sounded from heaven, and I dropped face down.
My great-grandfather Enoch came and stood beside me and said, “Why have you cried out to me so bitterly and with tears?

A command has gone out from the Lord against those who live on the dry ground, that their end is to be carried out, because they have learned all the secrets of the angels, all the violence of the satans and all their most secret powers, all the power of those who practice sorcery and spells, and the power of those who cast idols for the whole earth;
how silver comes from the dust of the earth, and how soft metal comes into being on the earth.
For lead and tin are not produced from the earth as the first is; there is a spring that produces them, and an angel stands in it, and that angel is prominent.”
After that my great-grandfather Enoch took me by the hand, raised me up, and said to me, “Go, for I have asked the Lord of Spirits about this upheaval on the earth.

He told me, ‘Because of their lawlessness their judgment has been decided, and I will not hold it back any longer. Because of the sorceries they have searched out and learned, the earth and its inhabitants will be destroyed.’

For these there will never be a place of repentance, because they have revealed what was hidden, and they are condemned. But as for you, my son, the Lord of Spirits knows that you are pure and innocent of this blame concerning the secrets.

He has set your name among the holy ones
and will keep you safe among those who live on the dry ground;
he has destined your righteous offspring for kingship and great honor,
and from your offspring will come a spring of the righteous and holy, past counting, forever.”

notes.text: *Noah*: Hebrew *Noaḥ*, connected in Gen 5:29 with *naḥam*, “to comfort,” and with *nuaḥ*, “to rest.” Chapters 65–69:25 are another piece of the Noah tradition (see the note at 54:7); Noah speaks in the first person.
Great-grandfather: so the sense; the text has “grandfather” (Ge'ez uses the word loosely). By Gen 5:21–29 Enoch is Noah’s great-grandfather: Enoch, Methuselah, Lamech, Noah.

verses.text: After that he showed me the angels of punishment who are ready to come and unleash all the forces of the water that lies under the earth, to bring judgment and destruction on all who live on the dry ground.
The Lord of Spirits ordered the angels who were going out not to raise the waters but to hold them back, for those angels were in charge of the forces of the waters.
Then I left Enoch’s presence.
In those days the word of God came to me, and he said to me, “Noah, your lot has come up before me, a lot free of blame, a lot of love and uprightness.

Now the angels are building a wooden structure,{a} and when they have finished the task I will lay my hand on it and keep it safe. From it will come the seed of life, and a change will take place, so that the earth will not be left empty.

I will establish your offspring before me forever and ever, and I will scatter abroad those who live with you. It will not be barren on the face of the dry ground, but it will be blessed and will multiply on the earth in the name of the Lord.”

He will lock up those angels who displayed lawlessness in that burning valley that my great-grandfather Enoch had shown me earlier in the west, near the mountains of gold, silver, iron, soft metal, and tin.{b}
I saw that valley, in which there was a great churning and a heaving of the waters.

When all this happened, from that fiery molten metal and from the churning in that place, a smell of sulfur arose and mixed with those waters. That valley of the angels who had led people astray burned beneath that ground.
Through its valleys flow rivers of fire, where those angels are punished who led astray the inhabitants of the dry ground.

But in those days those waters will serve the kings, the powerful, the exalted, and those who live on the dry ground for the healing of body and soul,{c} and for the punishment of the spirit. Their spirits are full of lust, so that they will be punished in their bodies, for they have denied the Lord of Spirits. They see their punishment every day, yet they do not believe in his name.
As the burning of their bodies grows fierce, a matching change will come over their spirits forever and ever, for no one will speak an idle word before the Lord of Spirits.
For judgment will come on them, because they trust in the lust of their bodies and deny the Spirit of the Lord.

Those same waters will change in those days. When those angels are punished in these waters, the springs will change their heat; and when the angels come up, the spring water will change and turn cold.
I heard Michael respond, “This judgment by which the angels are judged is a witness against the kings and the powerful who possess the dry ground.
For these waters of judgment serve the healing of the kings’ bodies and the lust of their bodies; so they will not see or believe that those waters will change and become a fire that burns forever.”

notes.text: A wooden structure: the ark (Gen 6:14–16). Here angels build it.
Compare 52:2 and 53:1; 54:1.

Healing of body and soul: so the manuscripts; Charles emends to “for the healing of the body, but for the punishment of the spirit.” The hot springs may allude to those used by Herod the Great at Callirrhoe by the Dead Sea, about 4 BC (Josephus, *Antiquities* 17.171–173).

verses.text: After that my great-grandfather Enoch instructed me in every secret contained in the book of the discourses that had been given to him, and he gathered them for me into the words of the book of the discourses.

On that day Michael spoke up and said to Raphael, “The force of the spirit carries me away and makes me tremble at the severity of the judgment of the secrets, the judgment of the angels. Who can bear the harsh judgment that has been carried out, before which they melt?”

Again Michael spoke up and said to Raphael, “Who would not be softened in heart about it, and whose insides would not be troubled by this word of judgment passed against them, against those whom they have led out like this?”

When he stood before the Lord of Spirits, Michael said to Raphael, “I will not take their side under the eye of the Lord, for the Lord of Spirits is angry with them because they behave as if they were the Lord.
That is why everything hidden will come upon them forever and ever. Neither angel nor human will have a share in it; they alone have received their judgment forever and ever.”
After this judgment they will terrify them and make them tremble, because they revealed this to those who live on the dry ground.

Here are the names of those angels.{a} The first of them is Semyaza; the second Artaqifa; the third Armen; the fourth Kokabel; the fifth Turael; the sixth Rumyal; the seventh Danyal; the eighth Neqael; the ninth Baraqel; the tenth Azazel; the eleventh Armaros; the twelfth Batryal; the thirteenth Basasael; the fourteenth Ananel; the fifteenth Turel; the sixteenth Simapesiel; the seventeenth Yetrel; the eighteenth Tumael; the nineteenth Turel; the twentieth Rumael; the twenty-first Azazel.
These are the leaders of their angels and their names, their chiefs over hundreds, over fifties, and over tens.
The name of the first is Yeqon.{b} He is the one who led all the children of God astray, brought them down to the earth, and misled them through the daughters of humankind.
The second is named Asbeel. He gave evil counsel to the holy children of God and misled them into defiling their bodies with human women.

The third is named Gadreel. He is the one who showed human beings every deadly blow. He led Eve astray,{c} and showed human beings the weapons of death: shield, breastplate, and sword for battle, and every weapon of death.
From his hand they have gone out against those who live on the dry ground from that day and forever.
The fourth is named Penemue. He taught human beings bitter and sweet, and taught them all the secrets of their wisdom.
He showed people how to write with ink and paper,{d} and through this many have sinned from age to age until this day.
Human beings were not created for this, to confirm their good faith with pen and ink.

For humans were created no differently from the angels, to stay righteous and pure, and death, which ruins everything, would not have touched them. But through this knowledge of theirs they are perishing, and through this power it is devouring me.{e}

The fifth is named Kasdeya. He showed human beings all the evil blows of spirits and demons: the blows that strike the embryo in the womb so that it miscarries, the bites of the snake, and the blows that come in the midday heat, the snake’s offspring, whose name is Tabaet.{f}
This is Kasbeel’s task: he is chief of the oath, which he disclosed to the holy ones while he dwelt in the glory on high; its name is Biqa.
This one asked Michael to show him the hidden name, so that he might pronounce it in the oath, so that those who revealed every secret thing to humankind would tremble before that name and oath.
Such is the force of this oath, mighty and strong. He put this oath, Akae, in Michael’s hand.

These are the secrets of this oath,
and they are made firm by his oath:
heaven was hung up before the world was created,
and forever.

By it the earth was founded on the water,
and from the hidden places of the mountains come lovely waters,
from the creation of the world and forever.

By that oath the depths are made fast;
they stay and do not move from their place, from age to age.

By that oath the sun and moon complete their courses
and do not swerve from their decree, from age to age.
So too the spirits of the water and of the winds, of all the breezes, and their paths from every quarter of the winds.
There the voices of the thunder and the light of the lightning are kept, and there the storerooms of the hail and of the frost are kept, the storerooms of the mist and of the rain and dew.

All of them believe and offer thanks to the Lord of Spirits and give him glory with all their might; their food is all thanksgiving. They thank, glorify, and exalt the Lord of Spirits’ name forever and ever.

He sat on his glorious throne,
and the whole of judgment was handed over to the Son of Man.{i}
He makes the sinners vanish and be destroyed from the face of the earth,
together with those who led the world astray.

They will be bound with chains
and locked up in the gathering place of their destruction,
and all their works will vanish from the face of the earth.

From then on nothing will be corruptible,
for that Son of Man has come into view
and is seated on his glorious throne.
All evil will pass away before him,
and the word of that Son of Man will go out
and prevail before the Lord of Spirits.
Here ends Enoch’s third discourse.

notes.text: This list largely repeats 6:7, in corrupted Ethiopic forms; compare the notes there. *Shemihazah* appears as *Semyaza*; *Asael* appears twice (as *Azazel*).

*Yeqon*: perhaps “he will incite” (Hebrew *yaqum*, “he rises”). *Asbeel*: perhaps “deserter from God.” *Gadreel*: “God is my helper” or “wall of God.” *Penemue*: perhaps “inside” or “face.” *Kasdeya*: “Chaldean,” recalling the Chaldeans as experts in magic and astrology. *Kasbeel*: perhaps “deceiver of God.” *Biqa*: perhaps “request” or “the one who asks.” *Akae*: meaning unknown; some connect it with *ʾ-k-y*, “to name.”
He led Eve astray: here the serpent of Gen 3 is identified with a fallen angel; compare Wis 2:24; Rev 12:9.
Paper: papyrus. Writing itself is here counted among the forbidden arts, in contrast to Enoch the scribe (12:4) and to Jubilees 4:17, where Enoch is the first to learn writing.
It is devouring me: perhaps “death is devouring us”; the text is uncertain.
Midday heat: compare Ps 91:6. *Tabaet*: perhaps “male” or “strong”; the meaning is uncertain.
Compare Job 38:8–11; Jer 5:22.
Compare Isa 40:26; Bar 3:34–35.
Compare John 5:22, 27.

verses.text: After this, while he was still alive, his name was lifted up into the presence of that Son of Man and into the presence of the Lord of Spirits, away from those who live on the dry ground.{a}
He was raised on the chariots of the wind,{b} and his name departed from among them.

From that day I was no longer counted among them. He set me between two winds, between north and west, where the angels had taken the cords to mark out for me a place for the chosen and the righteous.
There I saw the first ancestors and the righteous who from the beginning have lived in that place.

notes.text: Chapters 70–71 describe Enoch’s final removal from earth; compare Gen 5:24, “Enoch walked with God, and he was no more, for God took him.” The narrative shifts from third person (70:1–2) to first person (70:3).
The chariots of the wind: or “of the spirit”; compare Elijah in 2 Kgs 2:11.

verses.text:
He showed me all the secrets of the ends of heaven,
all the storerooms of all the stars and all the lights,
from where they come out before the holy ones.

I saw angels past counting,
thousands upon thousands and myriads upon myriads,
surrounding that house.
Michael, Raphael, Gabriel, and Phanuel,
and the holy angels in heaven above,
go in and out of that house.

Out of that house came Michael and Gabriel, Raphael and Phanuel,
and many holy angels beyond number,

and the Head of Days came with them,
his head pure and white like wool,
his robes past describing.

I fell on my face;
my whole body went limp,
and my spirit was transformed.
I cried out in a loud voice,
with a spirit of power,
and I blessed, glorified, and exalted.
These blessings that came from my mouth pleased that Head of Days.

That Head of Days came, accompanied by Michael, Gabriel, Raphael, and Phanuel,
and thousands and myriads of angels past counting.

He{d} came to me, greeted me with his voice, and said to me,
“You are that son of man{e} who was born for righteousness;
righteousness rests on you,
and the righteousness of the Head of Days will not abandon you.”

He said to me,
“He proclaims peace to you in the name of the age to come,
for from there peace has gone out since the creation of the world,
and so you will have it forever and ever and ever.

Everyone will walk in your ways,
since righteousness will never abandon you;
with you will be their homes, and with you their inheritance,
and they will not be parted from you forever and ever and ever.

So with that son of man there will be long life,
and the righteous will have peace and an upright way
in the Lord of Spirits’ name forever and ever.”

notes.text: The children of God: angels; compare 6:2; Job 1:6.
Hyacinth: a precious stone, probably blue (sapphire or jacinth).
Crystals: or “hailstones”; compare 14:9–10.
He: the angel, or perhaps the Head of Days himself. Charles assumes a passage has been lost before this verse and changes “you” to “this.”

You are that son of man: so all the Ethiopic manuscripts. Here Enoch himself is identified with the heavenly figure of the Parables, or, as many read it, is simply called “a human being born for righteousness” (compare 60:10). Charles and some translators emend to “This is the Son of Man.” This translation follows the manuscripts.
